entities.name: Conservation of Energy
entities.definition: Conservation of energy: for an isolated system the total energy — summed over all forms (kinetic, potential, thermal, chemical, nuclear, ...) — remains constant in time; energy transforms between forms but is neither created nor destroyed. Historical line: Mayer (1842), Joule (1843), Helmholtz (1847, 'Über die Erhaltung der Kraft'); standard statement per Halliday, Resnick, Walker 12th ed., Ch 8.

provenance.source: Halliday, Resnick, Walker, Fundamentals of Physics 12th ed., Ch 8 (potential energy and conservation of energy in isolated systems).

historical.stated_by: Julius Robert Mayer / Hermann von Helmholtz
historical.where: Helmholtz, Über die Erhaltung der Kraft

timeline.event: First statement of energy conservation (work-heat equivalence)
Über die Erhaltung der Kraft — formal statement of energy conservation

entities.name: first law of thermodynamics
entities.definition: The first law states that internal energy change equals heat added minus work done by the system. This principle establishes conservation of energy for any transition between equilibrium states.

provenance.source: University Physics Volume 2 (2016), OpenStax. Term locator: https://openstax.org/books/university-physics-volume-2/pages/3-key-terms. Used as a reference; definition independently phrased.

formal.statement: For a closed system, the change in internal energy equals the heat added to the system minus the work done by the system.

entities.name: Newton's Second Law
entities.definition: Newton's second law of motion: the net external force on a system equals the time rate of change of its total linear momentum, ΣF = dp/dt; for constant mass this reduces to F = m a. Valid in classical (non-relativistic) mechanics in inertial reference frames. Stated by Isaac Newton as Lex II in Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica (1687); standard modern formulation per Halliday, Resnick, Walker 12th ed., Ch 5.

provenance.source: Halliday, Resnick, Walker, Fundamentals of Physics 12th ed., Ch 5 (Newton second law, force and momentum); Principia (1687), Lex II.

entities.name: second law of thermodynamics
entities.definition: The second law dictates that total entropy never decreases in a spontaneous process. It implies the directionality of natural changes and limits the efficiency of heat engines.

provenance.source: Physics (2020), OpenStax. Term locator: https://openstax.org/books/physics/pages/12-key-terms. Used as a reference; definition independently phrased.
